Definition: apparently a comparative of the same as G712; the left hand (as second-best):--left (hand).
BiblicalUsage: The left hand is the weaker hand, the second-best side, and the New Testament uses it that way. Jesus tells us not to let the left hand know what the right hand is doing, James and John ask to sit at His right and His left in glory, and Paul speaks of the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the left hand matters because Jesus uses it to teach secrecy in giving: true generosity does not keep score, not even with itself. And I believe Paul's armour on both sides says the Christian is armed for every direction the fight comes from.
